A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCORER research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across v3's expanded sections and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original MinAtar and MiniGrid experiments, classic-control learning curves, sample-efficiency results, and SCORER ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds Atari-5, Baird's counterexample, Deep Sea, learning-rate sensitivity, and representation analyses.

M1.justification: The specified PQN vector-observation encoder gains a LayerNorm before ReLU, whereas v2 specifies normalization only after ReLU (v2 Table 11; v3 Table 13). This is a limited reported architectural revision. SCORER's leader/follower objectives, stop-gradient separation, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds Atari-5 pixel-control evaluation, Baird's off-policy counterexample, and deterministic and stochastic Deep Sea at depth 10. These substantially extend visual complexity, exploration requirements, and environmental conditions beyond v2's retained MinAtar, MiniGrid, and classic-control coverage.

E2.justification: v3 evaluates Linear TD in the new Baird experiment and Bootstrapped DQN in Deep Sea. It also adds monolithic DQN with faster encoder learning rates to the existing coupling comparison, directly testing an alternative explanation for SCORER's gains. The original benchmark comparator families remain; extending PQN to Atari alone is not a comparator addition.

E3.justification: MinAtar Table 1 changes from per-seed peak returns to averages over the final 10% of training. Appendix C revises PQN rollout length from 64 to 32, minibatch count from 8 to 32, exploration annealing from 80% to 40%, and tabulated clipping from 0.5 to 5.0. New Atari experiments use 200M frames per game. These establish reported protocol changes without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds direct divergence testing on Baird's counterexample, deterministic-versus-stochastic Deep Sea comparisons, follower learning-rate sensitivity, and Breakout representation-rank and parameter-norm diagnostics. The coupling ablation adds the faster-encoder control and per-environment comparisons. Existing role-assignment and follower-objective studies are retained.

E5.justification: v2's normal-approximation IQM confidence intervals and Welch tests are replaced by reported percentile-bootstrap intervals and IQM-difference tests using 2,000 resamples (v2 Appendix E; v3 Appendix F). Existing benchmark summaries retain 30 seeds. New Atari experiments specify five seeds per game, and Deep Sea specifies 30; no increase in runs for retained experiments is established.

E6.justification: Table 1 reports revised summaries: DDQN Breakout baseline/SCORER values change from 44.78/67.06 to 36.47/64.44 under the new metric, rather than representing same-setting performance changes. Old DQN rows also remain beside a second DQN block. New results include Atari gains on Phoenix and Qbert and stochastic Deep Sea solved rates near 100% versus roughly 20% for Bootstrapped DQN. MiniGrid threshold results and MinAtar sample-efficiency tables retain their values.

T1.justification: v3 adds the approximate aleatoric/epistemic variance decomposition in Equation 10 and explicitly identifies x* as the global optimum in the outer-convergence discussion and Theorem M.1. The assumptions, convergence bounds, and proof calculations from v2 Appendix J are otherwise retained in Appendix M; no new convergence proof accompanies these additions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: game-theoretic separation of perception and control, stabilization through two-timescale learning, and improved efficiency or returns without increased network capacity. The added experiments expand support without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: v3 newly explains stochastic robustness through reducible epistemic variance, discusses gradients of the sampled variance objective, and supplies an explicit optimization rationale for leader assignment. It acknowledges that faster encoder updates alone help and interprets early high representation rank as a possible stabilizing mechanism. Appendix L explicitly cautions that the observed association does not establish causality. Existing discrete-action and sample-complexity limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds Atari architecture and hyperparameter specifications, software dependencies, explicit baseline settings, and learning-rate and clipping explanations. Appendix A changes the code-access address from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. Documentation remains inconsistent: MinAtar PQN clipping is 0.5 in prose but 5.0 in Tables 6–7, and the general full-duration decay description conflicts with Table 6's first-half schedule.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds value-structure references and explicitly distinguishes SCORER from Anand and Precup's additive decompositions and Garcin et al.'s representation separation. Additional references support Atari-5, Deep Sea, bootstrap evaluation, and representation diagnostics. These refine the existing positioning without substantially reorganizing its relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language corrections, removes the duplicated Stackelberg-definition sentence, expands experimental and statistical explanations, and adds relevant subsections and appendices. Publication-header and acknowledgment text are added. The main narrative sequence, abstract, conclusion, and most method exposition remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Atari and stability figures, sensitivity and representation plots, per-environment coupling comparisons, and Atari configuration tables. Existing MinAtar and classic-control plots are redrawn, and the aggregate ablation display is revised. Appendix J redisplays the main Deep Sea results rather than adding another experiment. Table 1 also acquires the duplicated DQN block.

improvement.justification: The Atari-5 evaluation, direct stability and stochasticity tests, and matched faster-encoder control address important gaps in v2's empirical support for its central claims. Final-window scoring and bootstrap reporting also strengthen evaluation. These substantial gains outweigh the duplicated DQN rows in Table 1 and conflicting clipping/decay documentation in Appendix C, although those defects still limit reporting reliability and reproducibility.
